The appellant had filed an application (Registration No. SEBIH/R/P/24/00187) dated Nil (received by SEBI on August 17, 2024) under the Right to Information Act, 2005 (“RTI Act”). The respondent, by a letter dated August 27, 2024, responded to the application filed by the appellant. The appellant filed an appeal dated Nil (received by the Office of Appellate Authority on September 23, 2024). I have perused the application, the response of the respondent and the appeal and find that the matter can be decided based on the material available on record.\\n\\n2. **Request in the application**- The appellant, vide his application dated Nil, *inter alia*, has submitted that he had bought 500 shares of Leaprofin Securities Ltd, however, he is unable to get payment for the same as the registered office of the said company has been closed. The appellant has requested that he may be helped with respect to the aforesaid grievance.\\n\\n3. **Reply of the Respondent** - The respondent, in response to the application informed that the information sought is in the nature of grievance. Further, the respondent informed that taking action or resolution of grievance does not come under the provisions of RTI Act. Therefore, it does not qualify as information under provisions of section 2(f) of RTI Act. The respondent further informed that investor grievances may be lodged through SCORES and also provided the details of toll free helpline service <hi>number</hi> launched by SEBI to facilitate replies to various queries of the general public on matters relating to securities market\\n\\n4. **Ground of appeal** - On perusal of the appeal, it appears that the appellant is not satisfied with the response provided by the respondent.\\n\\nPage 1 of 2\\n\",\"source\":{\"docId\":\"clf-stininqvoxfvo82oaf7381ij\",\"title\":\"October2024/1729167665827.pdf\",\"url\":\"/cl/f767fe84-6cb8-45ae-99b4-b610f50d0cb6\",\"app\":\"KnowledgeBase\",\"page_title\":\"\",\"entity\":\"file\",\"itemId\":\"d48a2227-e540-44b9-88d6-29182964649d\",\"clId\":\"f767fe84-6cb8-45ae-99b4-b610f50d0cb6\"},\"confidence\":0.3000083292592606,\"visibleChunkIndices\":[3,1,2]},{\"id\":\"clf-sqerrb1n4t792vrpodxsn0rl\",\"content\":\"Source: Knowledge Base\\nFile: October2024/1729167594719.pdf\\nKnowledge Base ID: f767fe84-6cb8-45ae-99b4-b610f50d0cb6\\nMime Type: application/pdf\\nFile Size: 407026 bytes\\nCreated: 1h ago\\nUpdated At: 1h ago\\nUploaded By: officer1@xyne.local\\nContent: [3] Appeal No. 6170 of 2024\\n\\n4. **Ground of appeal** - The appellant filed the appeal on the ground that he was refused access to information requested.\\n\\n5. I have perused the aforesaid request and the response provided thereto. I concur with the response of the respondent that the queries in the application are vague and not specific. It is an established law that the information sought for in order to be disclosable under the RTI Act, must be clear, specific and available in the records of the public authority. In this context, I note that in the matter of *<hi>Mr</hi>. T. V. Sundaresan vs. CPIO, Securities and Exchange Board of India* (Decision dated November 24, 2021), the Hon’ble Central Information Commission (hereinafter referred to as “CIC”) held: “The framework of the RTI Act, 2005 expects that the information sought is specific and believed to be existing with the public authority in documented or material form as such; which can be shared with the appellant as per the provisions of the RTI Act. Answering to broad, multiple and general queries and presumptive documents that should have been generated as per the expectation of the appellant cannot be furnished under the provisions of the Act.” Accordingly, I do not find any deficiency in the response of the respondent.\\n\\n6. In view of the above observations, I find that there is no need to interfere with the decision of the respondent. The Appeal is accordingly dismissed.\\n\\nPlace: Mumbai  \\nDate: October 17, 2024\\n\\nRUCHI CHOJER  \\nAPPELLATE AUTHORITY UNDER THE RTI ACT  \\nSECURITIES AND EXCHANGE BOARD OF INDIA\\n\\nPage 2 of 2\\n[1] 1. If a public authority has any information in the form of data or analysed data, or abstracts, or statistics, an applicant may access such information, subject to the exemptions in section 8 of the Act. But where the information sought is not a part of the record of a public authority, and where such information is not required to be maintained under any law or the rules or regulations of the public authority, the Act does not cast an obligation upon the public authority, to collect or collate such non-available information and then furnish it to an applicant .' I have perused the application, the response of the respondent and the appeal and find that the matter can be decided based on the material available on record.\\n\\n2. **Request of the application** - The appellant vide his request of the application dated June 14, 2024, sought information related to Groww App.\\n\\n3. **Reply of the Respondent** - The respondent, in response to the application, informed that the information sought by applicant is not maintained by SEBI in normal course of regulation of securities market. do not call `searchKnowledgeBase` if the user only needs the listing.\n  - Partial-scope ask: if untargeted `ls` returns a folder root such as `Security`, call `ls({ target: { type: \"folder\", folderId: \"folder-security\" }, depth: 1, metadata: false })` to inspect inside it; do not infer collection-root access from that folder row.\n  - Filtered content ask: for \"answer only from PDF files in Security policies\", first call `ls({ target: { type: \"path\", collectionId: \"kb-1\", path: \"/Policies/Security\" }, depth: 2, metadata: true })`, keep only rows whose `mime_type` is PDF, then call `searchKnowledgeBase({ query: \"exception approval workflow\", filters: { targets: [{ type: \"file\", fileId: \"file-pdf-1\" }, { type: \"file\", fileId: \"file-pdf-2\" }] }, limit: 5 })`.\n  - Known scope ask: if the ask already names the exact KB location, call `searchKnowledgeBase({ query: \"contractor onboarding steps\", filters: { targets: [{ type: \"path\", collectionId: \"kb-1\", path: \"/HR/Onboarding/Checklist.md\" }] }, limit: 5 })`; skip `ls`.\n  - `ls` not useful: if the ask is not about KB, or the exact KB scope is already known and browsing will not improve precision, skip `ls`.\n\n### Public Agent Discipline\n- Call `list_custom_agents` before delegating; log the evaluation and expect it to return `null` when nobody qualifies.\n- Call `runPublicAgent` only after eliminating ambiguity about people, places, and time; restate the resolved entity info before invoking.\n- When list_custom_agents surfaces multiple strong candidates, compare them explicitly before deciding whether to delegate or to keep working with core tools.\n- Prioritize quality over latency; justify why the public agent is required and skip it when core tools can answer faster.\n- Document how the agent result ties back to the user goal and decide whether another follow-up is necessary before moving on.\n- Example: \"Confirmed ACME (US West, RevOps). runPublicAgent(agentName: \"renewal-navigator\", query: \"Summarize ACME renewals in Oct 2024 with blockers and owners\").\"\n\n### Agent Query Crafting\n- Pass explicit agent identifiers plus customized queries; craft one focused query per agent instead of reusing generic text.\n- Enrich queries with clarified scope, dates, and user intents gathered during reasoning to minimize back-and-forth.\n- Record every rewritten query in the reasoning log so reviewers can trace why that agent was triggered.\n- Example: \"runPublicAgent(agentId: \"sales-notes\", query: \"Detail Delta Airlines Q3 forecast confidence after verifying Delta == DAL GTM account\").\"\n\n### Execution Discipline\n- Show proactive drive: after each subtask plan, immediately schedule and run the necessary tools.\n- Combine sequential and parallel tool usage when safe; default to running more than one independent tool per turn.\n- Track dependencies explicitly so you never trigger a child tool before its parent results are analyzed.\n- Prefer the shortest correct tool path; do not insert browsing or discovery steps when a precise search can answer directly.\n\n### Chain-of-Thought Commitment\n- Plan first: picture the end-state, derive minimal subgoals, map tools to each, and weigh independence/dependencies against expected information gain, cost, and latency.\n- For every tool choice, mentally simulate parameter variants; verify schema/limit fit, broaden safe coverage (aliases/entities/scopes/time windows), and consolidate independent lookups into one turn without redundancy.\n- Before committing, run a quick pre-mortem for gaps/failure modes and pick the configuration that maximizes correct coverage per turn; revise if a superior valid parameterization emerges.\n- Examples:\n  - \"What does Alex say about Q4?\" — enumerate Alex identities first, gather IDs, then in one turn query Slack and Gmail with OR-expanded senders plus Q4 synonyms and bounded dates.\n  - \"Build an RCA timeline for last night's outage\" — skim Slack for SEV markers to extract incident keys, then in dependent turns hit Jira with exact keys and Calendar ±2h to stitch the timeline.\n\n### Internal Agent Discipline\n- Internal agents are built-in system agents that are ALWAYS available and do NOT require calling list_custom_agents.\n- Each internal agent provides specific capabilities beyond what core tools can offer.\n- Select internal agents based on capability match, not name familiarity.\n- Use internal agents when core tools or fragment-based retrieval are insufficient.\n- Always follow the expected input format defined for each agent.\n\n### Available Internal Agents\n- agentId: deep_document_agent\n  name: Deep Document Agent\n  capabilities: deep_document_analysis, document_summary, long_context_reading\n  description: Explores a single document intelligently using structured sampling and targeted reading to build a comprehensive understanding.\n  input_format: JSON { userQuery: string, docId: string, startingOffsets?: number[] }\n\n### Usage Guidelines\n- For internal agents: Use run_public_agent directly with the agentId from above.\n- Choose agents based on their capabilities and your task requirements.\n# PLANNING\n- Call toDoWrite at the start of a turn when the plan is new, when review requested changes, or when you need to add or close tasks; otherwise you may proceed without calling toDoWrite to avoid unnecessary iterations.\n- Terminate the active plan the moment you have enough evidence to cater to the complete requirement of the user; immediately drop any remaining subtasks when the goal is satisfied.\n- Scale the number of subtasks to the query’s true complexity , however quality of the final answer and complete execution and satisfaction of user's query outranks task count, you must always prioritize quality\n- Maintain one sub-task per concrete goal; list only the tools truly needed for that sub-task.\n- Only chain subtasks when real dependencies exist—for example, “fetch the people who messaged me today → gather the emails received from them → summarize the combined thread” keeps later steps paused until earlier outputs arrive.\n- After every tool run, immediately update the active sub-task’s status, result, and any newly required tasks so the plan mirrors reality.\n- Never finish a turn after only calling toDoWrite—run at least one execution tool that advances the active task.\n# EXECUTION STRATEGY\n- Work tasks sequentially; complete the current task before starting the next.\n- Call tools with precise parameters tied to the sub-task goal; reuse stored fragments instead of re-fetching data.\n- Run list_custom_agents before run_public_agent; document why the selected agent accelerates the plan.\n- Prefer list_custom_agents → run_public_agent before core tools when justified by the plan.\n- Invoke list_custom_agents at the sub-task level whenever targeted delegation could unlock better results; multi-part queries may require multiple calls as the context evolves.\n- Let earlier tool outputs reshape later sub-tasks (e.g., if getSlackRelatedMessages returns only Finance senders, rewrite the next list_custom_agents query with that Finance focus before proceeding).\n- Obey the `recommendation` flag: pause for clarifications when it reads `clarify_query`, keep collecting data for `gather_more`, and do not progress until a fresh plan is in place for `replan`.\n- If anomalies or notes in the latest review call out missing evidence, misalignments, or unresolved questions, fix those items before progressing and explain the remediation in the plan.\n\n# TOOL CALLS & EXPECTATIONS\n- Use the model's native function/tool-call interface. Provide clean JSON arguments.\n- Do NOT wrap tool calls in custom XML—JAF already handles execution.\n### Agent Delegation Guidelines\n- For INTERNAL agents (listed in system prompt): Use `run_public_agent` directly without calling `list_custom_agents`.\n- For CUSTOM agents (user-defined): MUST call `list_custom_agents` first to discover available agents.\n- If `list_custom_agents` returns `null`, explicitly log that no custom agent was suitable, then proceed with core tools or internal agents.\n- When selecting an agent, compare capabilities and justify why this specific agent is the best fit.\n- Only delegate when a specific agent's documented capabilities make it unquestionably suitable; otherwise keep iterating yourself.\n- After you decide which tools to call, emit a standalone expected-results block summarizing what each tool should achieve:\n<expected_results>\n[\n  {\n    \"toolName\": \"searchGlobal\",\n    \"goal\": \"Find Q4 ARR mentions\",\n    \"successCriteria\": [\"ARR keyword present\", \"Dated Q4\"],\n    \"failureSignals\": [\"No ARR context\"],\n    \"stopCondition\": \"After 2 unsuccessful searches\"\n  }\n]\n</expected_results>\n- Include one entry per tool invocation you intend to make. These expectations feed automatic review, so keep them specific and measurable.\n\n# CONSTRAINT HANDLING\n- When the user requests an action the available tools cannot execute, produce the closest actionable substitute (draft, checklist, instructions) so progress continues.\n- State the exact limitation and what manual follow-up the user must perform to finish.\n\n# FINAL SYNTHESIS\n- Once the run is agentic and research is complete, CALL `synthesize_final_answer` with optional `insightsUsefulForAnswering` guidance when it will help the final answer model emphasize the right conclusions or ordering. This tool composes and streams the response.\n- If the run never became agentic, answer directly instead of calling `synthesize_final_answer`.\n- After calling `synthesize_final_answer`, do not output another user-facing answer in the assistant turn."

The appellant had filed an application (Registration No. SEBIH/R/P/24/00187) dated Nil (received by SEBI on August 17, 2024) under the Right to Information Act, 2005 (“RTI Act”). The respondent, by a letter dated August 27, 2024, responded to the application filed by the appellant. The appellant filed an appeal dated Nil (received by the Office of Appellate Authority on September 23, 2024). I have perused the application, the response of the respondent and the appeal and find that the matter can be decided based on the material available on record.\\\\n\\\\n2. **Request in the application**- The appellant, vide his application dated Nil, *inter alia*, has submitted that he had bought 500 shares of Leaprofin Securities Ltd, however, he is unable to get payment for the same as the registered office of the said company has been closed. The appellant has requested that he may be helped with respect to the aforesaid grievance.\\\\n\\\\n3. **Reply of the Respondent** - The respondent, in response to the application informed that the information sought is in the nature of grievance. Further, the respondent informed that taking action or resolution of grievance does not come under the provisions of RTI Act. Therefore, it does not qualify as information under provisions of section 2(f) of RTI Act. The respondent further informed that investor grievances may be lodged through SCORES and also provided the details of toll free helpline service <hi>number</hi> launched by SEBI to facilitate replies to various queries of the general public on matters relating to securities market\\\\n\\\\n4. **Ground of appeal** - On perusal of the appeal, it appears that the appellant is not satisfied with the response provided by the respondent.\\\\n\\\\nPage 1 of 2\\\\n\\\",\\\"source\\\":{\\\"docId\\\":\\\"clf-stininqvoxfvo82oaf7381ij\\\",\\\"title\\\":\\\"October2024/1729167665827.pdf\\\",\\\"url\\\":\\\"/cl/f767fe84-6cb8-45ae-99b4-b610f50d0cb6\\\",\\\"app\\\":\\\"KnowledgeBase\\\",\\\"page_title\\\":\\\"\\\",\\\"entity\\\":\\\"file\\\",\\\"itemId\\\":\\\"d48a2227-e540-44b9-88d6-29182964649d\\\",\\\"clId\\\":\\\"f767fe84-6cb8-45ae-99b4-b610f50d0cb6\\\"},\\\"confidence\\\":0.3000083292592606,\\\"visibleChunkIndices\\\":[3,1,2]},{\\\"id\\\":\\\"clf-sqerrb1n4t792vrpodxsn0rl\\\",\\\"content\\\":\\\"Source: Knowledge Base\\\\nFile: October2024/1729167594719.pdf\\\\nKnowledge Base ID: f767fe84-6cb8-45ae-99b4-b610f50d0cb6\\\\nMime Type: application/pdf\\\\nFile Size: 407026 bytes\\\\nCreated: 1h ago\\\\nUpdated At: 1h ago\\\\nUploaded By: officer1@xyne.local\\\\nContent: [3] Appeal No. 6170 of 2024\\\\n\\\\n4. **Ground of appeal** - The appellant filed the appeal on the ground that he was refused access to information requested.\\\\n\\\\n5. I have perused the aforesaid request and the response provided thereto. I concur with the response of the respondent that the queries in the application are vague and not specific. It is an established law that the information sought for in order to be disclosable under the RTI Act, must be clear, specific and available in the records of the public authority. In this context, I note that in the matter of *<hi>Mr</hi>. T. V. Sundaresan vs. CPIO, Securities and Exchange Board of India* (Decision dated November 24, 2021), the Hon’ble Central Information Commission (hereinafter referred to as “CIC”) held: “The framework of the RTI Act, 2005 expects that the information sought is specific and believed to be existing with the public authority in documented or material form as such; which can be shared with the appellant as per the provisions of the RTI Act. Answering to broad, multiple and general queries and presumptive documents that should have been generated as per the expectation of the appellant cannot be furnished under the provisions of the Act.” Accordingly, I do not find any deficiency in the response of the respondent.\\\\n\\\\n6. In view of the above observations, I find that there is no need to interfere with the decision of the respondent. The Appeal is accordingly dismissed.\\\\n\\\\nPlace: Mumbai  \\\\nDate: October 17, 2024\\\\n\\\\nRUCHI CHOJER  \\\\nAPPELLATE AUTHORITY UNDER THE RTI ACT  \\\\nSECURITIES AND EXCHANGE BOARD OF INDIA\\\\n\\\\nPage 2 of 2\\\\n[1] 1. The respondent also provided the details of the toll free helpline service <hi>numbers</hi> launched by SEBI to facilitate replies to various queries of the general public on matters relating to securities market.\\\\n\\\\n4. **Ground of appeal** – The appellant has filed the appeal on the ground that he was refused access to information requested.\\\\n\\\\n5. I have perused the application and the response provided thereto. On consideration, I concur with the response of the respondent that query of the appellant is more in the nature of grievance/complaint. I note that redressal of grievance does not come under the purview of the RTI Act. In this context, I note that the Hon’ble Central Information Commission, in the matter of *<hi>Mr</hi>. Surendra Vishwakarma vs. President Secretariat* (Order dated April 29, 2016) observed that “*In this context, we note that the RTI Act cannot be used to make the respondent to do certain things or take certain action for the reason that the Act is not the proper law for redressal of grievances/disputes and there are other appropriate forum(s) for resolving such matters.*” Notwithstanding the same, I note that the respondent has appropriately guided the appellant to refer to the SCORES website for lodging his grievance, if any, and also provided helpline service <hi>numbers</hi> launched by SEBI, to facilitate replies to various queries of the general public on matters relating to securities market. In view of the same, I find that the application has been adequately addressed and no further intervention is warranted at this stage.\\\\n\\\\n6. In view of the above observations, I find that there is no need to interfere with the decision of the respondent. The appellant had filed an application dated May 27, 2025 (received by the respondent through RTI MIS Portal) under the Right to Information Act, 2005 (' RTI Act '). The respondent, by a letter dated June 18, 2025,  responded  to  the  application  filed  by  the  appellant.  The  appellant  filed  an  appeal  (Reg.  No. SEBIH/A/E/25/00184) dated July 19, 2025. Query in the application - The appellant, in his application dated May 27, 2025, sought the following information:\\\\n' We wanted to ask something about our mutual fund from Groww customer support staff, but the customer support staff whose name was Anjali started giving evasive answers, then we asked her to talk to her senior, then she started talking rudely to me.\\\\nWhen we complained to Groww, we were told that they have taken action against their customer support staff, when we asked what action have you taken against your customer support staff, they said that they will not tell us\\\\nWhen we said that it is the customer right, they started threatening us through phone.'\\\\n3. Reply of the Respondent -The respondent, in response to the application, informed that the information sought is in the nature of complaint and is in the nature of seeking clarification. Accordingly, the same cannot be construed as \\\\\\\"information\\\\\\\", as defined u/s 2(f) of the RTI Act.\\\\nAdditionally, the respondent provided information regarding lodging of grievance, if any, on the SCORES portal of SEBI and tracking the status of the same. I have perused the application and the response provided thereto. On consideration, I concur with the response of the respondent that query of the appellant is more in the nature of grievance/complaint. I note that redressal of grievance does not come under the purview of the RTI Act. In this context, I note that the Hon'ble Central Information Commission, in the matter of <hi>Mr</hi>. Surendra Vishwakarma vs. President Secretariat (Order dated April 29, 2016) observed that ' In this context, we note that the RTI Act cannot be used to make the respondent to do certain things or take certain action for the reason that the Act is not the proper law for redressal of grievances/disputes and there are other appropriate forum(s) for resolving such matters .' Notwithstanding the same, I note that the respondent has appropriately guided the appellant to refer to the SCORES website for lodging his grievance, if any, and also provided helpline service <hi>numbers</hi> launched by SEBI, to facilitate replies to various queries of the general public on matters relating to securities market. In view of the same, I find that the application has been adequately addressed and no further intervention is warranted at this stage.\\\\n6. This is clear from a combined reading of section  3 and the definitions of `information' and `right to information' under clauses (f) and (j) of section 2 of the Act. If a public authority has any information in the form of data or analysed data, or abstracts, or statistics, an applicant may access such information, subject to the exemptions in section 8 of the Act. But where the information sought is not a part of the record of a public authority, and where such information is not required to be maintained under any law or the rules or regulations of the public authority, the Act does not cast an obligation upon the public authority, to collect or collate such non-available information and then furnish it to an applicant .' Accordingly, I do not find any deficiency in the response of the respondent.\\\\n6. In view of the above observations, I find that there is no need to interfere with the decision of the respondent. Securities  and  Exchange  Board  of  India  (hereinafter  referred  to  as SEBI ) conducted examination in the matter of delay in intimation of regulatory status by Wilmington Trust Collective  Investment  Trust  -  Lazard/Wilmington  ACW Ex-US  Equity  Advantage  Fund (hereinafter  referred  to  as 'Noticee' / 'applicant' ) to  check  compliance  with  provisions  of  SEBI  (Foreign  Portfolio Investors)  Regulations,  2019  (hereinafter  referred  to  as  ' FPI  Regulations, 2019 ') and applicable Circulars for the period beginning from April 28, 2023 till July  11,  2023  (hereinafter  referred  to  as  ' the  examination  period '  /  ' EP '). During examination, following was observed:\\n2. 1.1.  The applicant had not intimated the change in the regulatory status, Category and Sub-Category of the FPI, within seven working days to SEBI or Designated Depository Participant (DDP).\\n3. 1.2.  The applicant made fresh purchases before the completion of additional KYC requirements without holding a valid registration certificate.\\n2. Under Regulation 22(1)(c) of FPI Regulations, 2019 read with Clause 14 of Part A of the Master Circular for Foreign Portfolio Investors, Designated Depository Participants and Eligible Foreign Investors, dated December 19, 2022, if there is any change in the material information previously furnished by the FPI to the DDP and/or SEBI, which has a bearing on the certificate granted by the DDP on behalf  of  the  Board  or  change  in  regulatory  status,  change  in  category/  sub-\\n- category of the FPI, it shall as soon as possible but not later than seven working days inform the DDP and/or the Board in writing. As per Regulation 22(1)(a) of the FPI Regulations, 2019 read with Clause 13 of Part A of Master Circular dated December  19,  2022,  if  an  FPI  registered  under  a  particular  category/  subcategory fails to comply with applicable eligibility requirements, it shall promptly notify this change to its DDP to be reclassified under appropriate category/subcategory. As per Regulation 7(5) of the FPI Regulations, 2019, foreign portfolio investor is required to have a valid registration as long as it is holding securities or derivatives in India. Regulation 3(1) of the FPI Regulations, 2019 states that no person shall buy, sell or otherwise deal in securities as a foreign portfolio investor unless it has obtained a certificate granted by a designated depository participant on behalf of the Board.\\n3. Pursuant to above, adjudication proceedings were initiated and the competent authority appointed the undersigned as the Adjudicating Officer (AO) vide Order dated April 10, 2024 under Section 15-I of SEBI Act, 1992 and Rule 3 of SEBI (Procedure for Holding Inquiry and Imposing Penalties) Rules, 1995 (hereinafter referred to as ' SEBI Adjudication Rules ')  to  inquire  into  and  adjudge  under Section 15A(b) and Section 15HB of the SEBI Act, 1992 for the alleged violation of provisions of Regulation 22(1)(c) of FPI Regulations, 2019 read with Clause 14 of Part A of the Master Circular for Foreign Portfolio Investors, Designated Depository  Participants  and  Eligible  Foreign  Investors,  dated  December  19, 2022;  Regulation  3(1),  Regulation  7(5)  read  with  Regulation  5(a)  of  FPI Regulations, 2019 and Regulation 22(1)(a) of FPI Regulations, 2019 read with Clause 13 of Part A of Master Circular dated December 19, 2022; and Clause 5 of  Third  Schedule  of  Code  of  Conduct  read  with  Regulation  23  of  FPI Regulations, 2019.\\n4. A Show Cause Notice (hereafter referred to as ' SCN ') dated April 23, 2024 was issued  to  the  Applicant  in  terms  of  the  provisions  of  Rule  4(1)  of  the  SEBI Adjudication Rules, calling upon the Applicant to show cause as to why an inquiry should not be held and penalty be not imposed upon it, under Section 15A(b)\\nand Section 15HB of the SEBI Act, 1992, as applicable for the alleged violations of the aforesaid provisions.\\n[2] 5. Pending Adjudication Proceedings, the Applicant proposed to settle the instant proceedings initiated against it, without admitting or denying the findings of facts and  conclusions  of  law,  through  a  settlement  order  and  filed  a  settlement application with SEBI bearing Settlement Application No. 7950/2024 dated June 20, 2024,  in terms  of the  provisions  of  SEBI  (Settlement  Proceedings) Regulations, 2018 (hereinafter referred to as ' Settlement Regulations ').\\n6. The  Internal  Committee  (IC)  meeting  was  held  on  August  13,  2024.  Factors enumerated  under  Regulation  10  and  Schedule  II  of SEBI  (Settlement Proceedings)  Regulations,  2018  were  considered  by  the  IC.  The  Internal Committee (IC) recommended ₹64,35,000/- (Rupees Sixty-Four Lakh and ThirtyFive  Thousand  Only)  as  the  monetary  settlement  term.  The  applicant  also submitted  the  revised  settlement  terms  on  August  27,  2024,  in  line  with  the monetary term formulated by the IC. Consequently, the IC recommended the case for settlement. The application was subsequently placed before the High Powered  Advisory  Committee  (HPAC)  on  September  06,  2024.  The  HPAC agreed with the recommendations of the IC and recommended that the request of the applicant for settlement may be accepted.\\n7. The Panel of Whole Time Members of SEBI approved the said recommendation of the HPAC on November 06, 2024 and the same was communicated by SEBI to the applicant on November 08, 2024.\\n8. Subsequently, the applicant vide email dated November 14, 2024 informed about the remittance of the settlement amount, the receipt of which is confirmed.\\n9. Therefore, in view of the acceptance of the settlement terms and the receipt of settlement  amount  as  above  by  SEBI,  the  instant  adjudication  proceedings initiated against Wilmington Trust Collective Investment Trust -\\nSettlement Order in respect of Wilmington Trust Collective Investment Trust Lazard/Wilmington ACW Ex-US Equity Advantage Fund\\n- Lazard/Wilmington ACW Ex-US Equity Advantage Fund is disposed of in terms of  section  15JB  of  the  SEBI  Act  read  with  regulation  23(1)  of  the  Settlement Regulations on the basis of the settlement terms.\\n10. This order is without prejudice to the right of SEBI to take enforcement actions, in  terms of regulation 28 of the Settlement Regulations, including restoring or initiating the proceedings in respect to which the settlement order was passed against the applicant, if:\\n- i.  it comes to the notice of the Board that the applicant has not made full and true disclosure;\\n- ii.  applicant has violated the undertakings or waivers:\\n11. 24,  2003  to  enable  certain  entities  to  obtain guidance  from  the  Securities  and  Exchange  Board  of  India  (' Board ')  on  the applicability of laws and regulations administered by it, in Scheme, 2025.\\nIn view of the same, with effect from December 01, 2025, the processing of all informal guidance applications shall be governed by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Informal Guidance) Scheme, 2025 ( 'IG Scheme, 2025' ), which broadens the scope of the Scheme  and  enables stock exchanges, clearing corporations, depositories and Managers of Pooled Investment Vehicles registered with the Board, to seek guidance from the Board.\\nIt also envisages streamlining and structuring of the process for seeking guidance from the Board, by creation of a nodal cell for processing all informal guidance applications. To undertake capacity building, development and enhancement of skills of officers of SEBI in the fields of digital forensic, forensic accounting, cyber security etc.\\n2.  To design specially tailored courses / training program for SEBI officers to enhance their efficiency and overall output.\\n3.  To organize training, seminars, conferences and workshops on topics of mutual interest and invite each other's officers / faculties to participate.\\n4.  To use the expertise, facilities and resources available to enhance efficiency and overall output.\\n5. justify why the public agent is required and skip it when core tools can answer faster.\n- Document how the agent result ties back to the user goal and decide whether another follow-up is necessary before moving on.\n- Example: \"Confirmed ACME (US West, RevOps). runPublicAgent(agentName: \"renewal-navigator\", query: \"Summarize ACME renewals in Oct 2024 with blockers and owners\").\"\n\n### Agent Query Crafting\n- Pass explicit agent identifiers plus customized queries; craft one focused query per agent instead of reusing generic text.\n- Enrich queries with clarified scope, dates, and user intents gathered during reasoning to minimize back-and-forth.\n- Record every rewritten query in the reasoning log so reviewers can trace why that agent was triggered.\n- Example: \"runPublicAgent(agentId: \"sales-notes\", query: \"Detail Delta Airlines Q3 forecast confidence after verifying Delta == DAL GTM account\").\"\n\n### Execution Discipline\n- Show proactive drive: after each subtask plan, immediately schedule and run the necessary tools.\n- Combine sequential and parallel tool usage when safe; default to running more than one independent tool per turn.\n- Track dependencies explicitly so you never trigger a child tool before its parent results are analyzed.\n- Prefer the shortest correct tool path; do not insert browsing or discovery steps when a precise search can answer directly.\n\n### Chain-of-Thought Commitment\n- Plan first: picture the end-state, derive minimal subgoals, map tools to each, and weigh independence/dependencies against expected information gain, cost, and latency.\n- For every tool choice, mentally simulate parameter variants; verify schema/limit fit, broaden safe coverage (aliases/entities/scopes/time windows), and consolidate independent lookups into one turn without redundancy.\n- Before committing, run a quick pre-mortem for gaps/failure modes and pick the configuration that maximizes correct coverage per turn; revise if a superior valid parameterization emerges.\n- Examples:\n  - \"What does Alex say about Q4?\" — enumerate Alex identities first, gather IDs, then in one turn query Slack and Gmail with OR-expanded senders plus Q4 synonyms and bounded dates.\n  - \"Build an RCA timeline for last night's outage\" — skim Slack for SEV markers to extract incident keys, then in dependent turns hit Jira with exact keys and Calendar ±2h to stitch the timeline.\n\n### Internal Agent Discipline\n- Internal agents are built-in system agents that are ALWAYS available and do NOT require calling list_custom_agents.\n- Each internal agent provides specific capabilities beyond what core tools can offer.\n- Select internal agents based on capability match, not name familiarity.\n- Use internal agents when core tools or fragment-based retrieval are insufficient.\n- Always follow the expected input format defined for each agent.\n\n### Available Internal Agents\n- agentId: deep_document_agent\n  name: Deep Document Agent\n  capabilities: deep_document_analysis, document_summary, long_context_reading\n  description: Explores a single document intelligently using structured sampling and targeted reading to build a comprehensive understanding.\n  input_format: JSON { userQuery: string, docId: string, startingOffsets?: number[] }\n\n### Usage Guidelines\n- For internal agents: Use run_public_agent directly with the agentId from above.\n- Choose agents based on their capabilities and your task requirements.\n# PLANNING\n- Call toDoWrite at the start of a turn when the plan is new, when review requested changes, or when you need to add or close tasks; otherwise you may proceed without calling toDoWrite to avoid unnecessary iterations.\n- Terminate the active plan the moment you have enough evidence to cater to the complete requirement of the user; immediately drop any remaining subtasks when the goal is satisfied.\n- Scale the number of subtasks to the query’s true complexity , however quality of the final answer and complete execution and satisfaction of user's query outranks task count, you must always prioritize quality\n- Maintain one sub-task per concrete goal; list only the tools truly needed for that sub-task.\n- Only chain subtasks when real dependencies exist—for example, “fetch the people who messaged me today → gather the emails received from them → summarize the combined thread” keeps later steps paused until earlier outputs arrive.\n- After every tool run, immediately update the active sub-task’s status, result, and any newly required tasks so the plan mirrors reality.\n- Never finish a turn after only calling toDoWrite—run at least one execution tool that advances the active task.\n# EXECUTION STRATEGY\n- Work tasks sequentially; complete the current task before starting the next.\n- Call tools with precise parameters tied to the sub-task goal; reuse stored fragments instead of re-fetching data.\n- Run list_custom_agents before run_public_agent; document why the selected agent accelerates the plan.\n- Prefer list_custom_agents → run_public_agent before core tools when justified by the plan.\n- Invoke list_custom_agents at the sub-task level whenever targeted delegation could unlock better results; multi-part queries may require multiple calls as the context evolves.\n- Let earlier tool outputs reshape later sub-tasks (e.g., if getSlackRelatedMessages returns only Finance senders, rewrite the next list_custom_agents query with that Finance focus before proceeding).\n- Obey the `recommendation` flag: pause for clarifications when it reads `clarify_query`, keep collecting data for `gather_more`, and do not progress until a fresh plan is in place for `replan`.\n- If anomalies or notes in the latest review call out missing evidence, misalignments, or unresolved questions, fix those items before progressing and explain the remediation in the plan.\n\n# TOOL CALLS & EXPECTATIONS\n- Use the model's native function/tool-call interface. Provide clean JSON arguments.\n- Do NOT wrap tool calls in custom XML—JAF already handles execution.\n### Agent Delegation Guidelines\n- For INTERNAL agents (listed in system prompt): Use `run_public_agent` directly without calling `list_custom_agents`.\n- For CUSTOM agents (user-defined): MUST call `list_custom_agents` first to discover available agents.\n- If `list_custom_agents` returns `null`, explicitly log that no custom agent was suitable, then proceed with core tools or internal agents.\n- When selecting an agent, compare capabilities and justify why this specific agent is the best fit.\n- Only delegate when a specific agent's documented capabilities make it unquestionably suitable; otherwise keep iterating yourself.\n- After you decide which tools to call, emit a standalone expected-results block summarizing what each tool should achieve:\n<expected_results>\n[\n  {\n    \"toolName\": \"searchGlobal\",\n    \"goal\": \"Find Q4 ARR mentions\",\n    \"successCriteria\": [\"ARR keyword present\", \"Dated Q4\"],\n    \"failureSignals\": [\"No ARR context\"],\n    \"stopCondition\": \"After 2 unsuccessful searches\"\n  }\n]\n</expected_results>\n- Include one entry per tool invocation you intend to make. These expectations feed automatic review, so keep them specific and measurable.\n\n# CONSTRAINT HANDLING\n- When the user requests an action the available tools cannot execute, produce the closest actionable substitute (draft, checklist, instructions) so progress continues.\n- State the exact limitation and what manual follow-up the user must perform to finish.\n\n# FINAL SYNTHESIS\n- Once the run is agentic and research is complete, CALL `synthesize_final_answer` with optional `insightsUsefulForAnswering` guidance when it will help the final answer model emphasize the right conclusions or ordering. This tool composes and streams the response.\n- If the run never became agentic, answer directly instead of calling `synthesize_final_answer`.\n- After calling `synthesize_final_answer`, do not output another user-facing answer in the assistant turn."

The appellant had filed an application (Registration No. SEBIH/R/P/24/00187) dated Nil (received by SEBI on August 17, 2024) under the Right to Information Act, 2005 (“RTI Act”). The respondent, by a letter dated August 27, 2024, responded to the application filed by the appellant. The appellant filed an appeal dated Nil (received by the Office of Appellate Authority on September 23, 2024). I have perused the application, the response of the respondent and the appeal and find that the matter can be decided based on the material available on record.\\\\n\\\\n2. **Request in the application**- The appellant, vide his application dated Nil, *inter alia*, has submitted that he had bought 500 shares of Leaprofin Securities Ltd, however, he is unable to get payment for the same as the registered office of the said company has been closed. The appellant has requested that he may be helped with respect to the aforesaid grievance.\\\\n\\\\n3. **Reply of the Respondent** - The respondent, in response to the application informed that the information sought is in the nature of grievance. Further, the respondent informed that taking action or resolution of grievance does not come under the provisions of RTI Act. Therefore, it does not qualify as information under provisions of section 2(f) of RTI Act. The respondent further informed that investor grievances may be lodged through SCORES and also provided the details of toll free helpline service <hi>number</hi> launched by SEBI to facilitate replies to various queries of the general public on matters relating to securities market\\\\n\\\\n4. **Ground of appeal** - On perusal of the appeal, it appears that the appellant is not satisfied with the response provided by the respondent.\\\\n\\\\nPage 1 of 2\\\\n\\\",\\\"source\\\":{\\\"docId\\\":\\\"clf-stininqvoxfvo82oaf7381ij\\\",\\\"title\\\":\\\"October2024/1729167665827.pdf\\\",\\\"url\\\":\\\"/cl/f767fe84-6cb8-45ae-99b4-b610f50d0cb6\\\",\\\"app\\\":\\\"KnowledgeBase\\\",\\\"page_title\\\":\\\"\\\",\\\"entity\\\":\\\"file\\\",\\\"itemId\\\":\\\"d48a2227-e540-44b9-88d6-29182964649d\\\",\\\"clId\\\":\\\"f767fe84-6cb8-45ae-99b4-b610f50d0cb6\\\"},\\\"confidence\\\":0.3000083292592606,\\\"visibleChunkIndices\\\":[3,1,2]},{\\\"id\\\":\\\"clf-sqerrb1n4t792vrpodxsn0rl\\\",\\\"content\\\":\\\"Source: Knowledge Base\\\\nFile: October2024/1729167594719.pdf\\\\nKnowledge Base ID: f767fe84-6cb8-45ae-99b4-b610f50d0cb6\\\\nMime Type: application/pdf\\\\nFile Size: 407026 bytes\\\\nCreated: 1h ago\\\\nUpdated At: 1h ago\\\\nUploaded By: officer1@xyne.local\\\\nContent: [3] Appeal No. 6170 of 2024\\\\n\\\\n4. **Ground of appeal** - The appellant filed the appeal on the ground that he was refused access to information requested.\\\\n\\\\n5. I have perused the aforesaid request and the response provided thereto. I concur with the response of the respondent that the queries in the application are vague and not specific. It is an established law that the information sought for in order to be disclosable under the RTI Act, must be clear, specific and available in the records of the public authority. In this context, I note that in the matter of *<hi>Mr</hi>. T. V. Sundaresan vs. CPIO, Securities and Exchange Board of India* (Decision dated November 24, 2021), the Hon’ble Central Information Commission (hereinafter referred to as “CIC”) held: “The framework of the RTI Act, 2005 expects that the information sought is specific and believed to be existing with the public authority in documented or material form as such; which can be shared with the appellant as per the provisions of the RTI Act. Answering to broad, multiple and general queries and presumptive documents that should have been generated as per the expectation of the appellant cannot be furnished under the provisions of the Act.” Accordingly, I do not find any deficiency in the response of the respondent.\\\\n\\\\n6. In view of the above observations, I find that there is no need to interfere with the decision of the respondent. The Appeal is accordingly dismissed.\\\\n\\\\nPlace: Mumbai  \\\\nDate: October 17, 2024\\\\n\\\\nRUCHI CHOJER  \\\\nAPPELLATE AUTHORITY UNDER THE RTI ACT  \\\\nSECURITIES AND EXCHANGE BOARD OF INDIA\\\\n\\\\nPage 2 of 2\\\\n[1] 1. I have perused the application and the response provided thereto. On consideration, I concur with the response of the respondent that query of the appellant is more in the nature of grievance/complaint. I note that redressal of grievance does not come under the purview of the RTI Act. In this context, I note that the Hon’ble Central Information Commission, in the matter of *<hi>Mr</hi>. Surendra Vishwakarma vs. President Secretariat* (Order dated April 29, 2016) observed that “*In this context, we note that the RTI Act cannot be used to make the respondent to do certain things or take certain action for the reason that the Act is not the proper law for redressal of grievances/disputes and there are other appropriate forum(s) for resolving such matters.*” Notwithstanding the same, I note that the respondent has appropriately guided the appellant to refer to the SCORES website for lodging his grievance, if any, and also provided helpline service <hi>numbers</hi> launched by SEBI, to facilitate replies to various queries of the general public on matters relating to securities market. In view of the same, I find that the application has been adequately addressed and no further intervention is warranted at this stage.\\\\n\\\\n6. In view of the above observations, I find that there is no need to interfere with the decision of the respondent. The appeal is accordingly dismissed.\\\\n\\\\nPlace: Mumbai  \\\\nDate: August 12, 2025\\\\n\\\\nRUCHI CHOJER  \\\\nAPPELLATE AUTHORITY UNDER THE RTI ACT  \\\\nSECURITIES AND EXCHANGE BOARD OF INDIA\\\\n\\\\nPage 2 of 2\\\\n[1] 1. The appellant had filed an application dated May 27, 2025 (received by the respondent through RTI MIS Portal) under the Right to Information Act, 2005 (' RTI Act '). The respondent, by a letter dated June 18, 2025,  responded  to  the  application  filed  by  the  appellant.  The  appellant  filed  an  appeal  (Reg.  No. SEBIH/A/E/25/00184) dated July 19, 2025.  I have perused the application and the appeal and find that the matter can be decided based on the material available on record.\\\\n2. Query in the application - The appellant, in his application dated May 27, 2025, sought the following information:\\\\n' We wanted to ask something about our mutual fund from Groww customer support staff, but the customer support staff whose name was Anjali started giving evasive answers, then we asked her to talk to her senior, then she started talking rudely to me.\\\\nWhen we complained to Groww, we were told that they have taken action against their customer support staff, when we asked what action have you taken against your customer support staff, they said that they will not tell us\\\\nWhen we said that it is the customer right, they started threatening us through phone.'\\\\n3. Reply of the Respondent -The respondent, in response to the application, informed that the information sought is in the nature of complaint and is in the nature of seeking clarification. Accordingly, the same cannot be construed as \\\\\\\"information\\\\\\\", as defined u/s 2(f) of the RTI Act.\\\\nAdditionally, the respondent provided information regarding lodging of grievance, if any, on the SCORES portal of SEBI and tracking the status of the same. The respondent also provided the details of the toll free helpline service <hi>numbers</hi> launched by SEBI to facilitate replies to various queries of the general public on matters relating to securities market.\\\\n4. Ground of appeal -  The  appellant  has  filed  the  appeal  on  the  ground  that  he  was  refused  access  to information requested.\\\\n5. I have perused the application and the response provided thereto. On consideration, I concur with the response of the respondent that query of the appellant is more in the nature of grievance/complaint. I note that redressal of grievance does not come under the purview of the RTI Act. In this context, I note that the Hon'ble Central Information Commission, in the matter of <hi>Mr</hi>. Surendra Vishwakarma vs. President Secretariat (Order dated April 29, 2016) observed that ' In this context, we note that the RTI Act cannot be used to make the respondent to do certain things or take certain action for the reason that the Act is not the proper law for redressal of grievances/disputes and there are other appropriate forum(s) for resolving such matters .' Notwithstanding the same, I note that the respondent has appropriately guided the appellant to refer to the SCORES website for lodging his grievance, if any, and also provided helpline service <hi>numbers</hi> launched by SEBI, to facilitate replies to various queries of the general public on matters relating to securities market. In view of the same, I find that the application has been adequately addressed and no further intervention is warranted at this stage.\\\\n6. In  view  of  the  above  observations,  I  find  that  there  is  no  need  to  interfere  with  the  decision  of  the respondent. The appeal is accordingly dismissed.\\\\nPlace: Mumbai\\\\nDate: August 12, 2025\\\\nRUCHI CHOJER APPELLATE AUTHORITY UNDER THE RTI ACT SECURITIES AND EXCHANGE BOARD OF INDIA\\\\n\\\",\\\"source\\\":{\\\"docId\\\":\\\"clf-kk7l7ow5dxod6u49qpfs7jd9\\\",\\\"title\\\":\\\"August2025/1754997986010.pdf\\\",\\\"url\\\":\\\"/cl/35f2cc67-5994-4485-8e9e-f340b15d4c32\\\",\\\"app\\\":\\\"KnowledgeBase\\\",\\\"page_title\\\":\\\"\\\",\\\"entity\\\":\\\"file\\\",\\\"itemId\\\":\\\"168a0f1f-f5b5-4016-9ee2-f689b5cc86c0\\\",\\\"clId\\\":\\\"35f2cc67-5994-4485-8e9e-f340b15d4c32\\\"},\\\"confidence\\\":0.2958451791351243,\\\"visibleChunkIndices\\\":[3,1]},{\\\"id\\\":\\\"clf-hazy395o8rvo5y9umccokwyl\\\",\\\"content\\\":\\\"Source: Knowledge Base\\\\nFile: May2025/1747138050671.pdf\\\\nKnowledge Base ID: 4596312b-285e-40e1-97f4-9d1f4118fc3b\\\\nMime Type: application/pdf\\\\nFile Size: 405750 bytes\\\\nCreated: 3h ago\\\\nUpdated At: 3h ago\\\\nUploaded By: officer1@xyne.local\\\\nContent: [3] Appeal No. 5964 of 2024\\\\n\\\\n4. **Ground of appeal** - The appellant has filed the appeal on the ground that she has been provided incomplete, misleading and false information.\\\\n\\\\n5. This is clear from a combined reading of section  3 and the definitions of `information' and `right to information' under clauses (f) and (j) of section 2 of the Act. If a public authority has any information in the form of data or analysed data, or abstracts, or statistics, an applicant may access such information, subject to the exemptions in section 8 of the Act. But where the information sought is not a part of the record of a public authority, and where such information is not required to be maintained under any law or the rules or regulations of the public authority, the Act does not cast an obligation upon the public authority, to collect or collate such non-available information and then furnish it to an applicant .' Securities  and  Exchange  Board  of  India  (hereinafter  referred  to  as SEBI ) conducted examination in the matter of delay in intimation of regulatory status by Wilmington Trust Collective  Investment  Trust  -  Lazard/Wilmington  ACW Ex-US  Equity  Advantage  Fund (hereinafter  referred  to  as 'Noticee' / 'applicant' ) to  check  compliance  with  provisions  of  SEBI  (Foreign  Portfolio Investors)  Regulations,  2019  (hereinafter  referred  to  as  ' FPI  Regulations, 2019 ') and applicable Circulars for the period beginning from April 28, 2023 till July  11,  2023  (hereinafter  referred  to  as  ' the  examination  period '  /  ' EP '). During examination, following was observed:\\\\n2. 1.1.  The applicant had not intimated the change in the regulatory status, Category and Sub-Category of the FPI, within seven working days to SEBI or Designated Depository Participant (DDP).\\\\n3. 1.2.  The applicant made fresh purchases before the completion of additional KYC requirements without holding a valid registration certificate.\\\\n2. Under Regulation 22(1)(c) of FPI Regulations, 2019 read with Clause 14 of Part A of the Master Circular for Foreign Portfolio Investors, Designated Depository Participants and Eligible Foreign Investors, dated December 19, 2022, if there is any change in the material information previously furnished by the FPI to the DDP and/or SEBI, which has a bearing on the certificate granted by the DDP on behalf  of  the  Board  or  change  in  regulatory  status,  change  in  category/  sub-\\\\n- category of the FPI, it shall as soon as possible but not later than seven working days inform the DDP and/or the Board in writing. As per Regulation 22(1)(a) of the FPI Regulations, 2019 read with Clause 13 of Part A of Master Circular dated December  19,  2022,  if  an  FPI  registered  under  a  particular  category/  subcategory fails to comply with applicable eligibility requirements, it shall promptly notify this change to its DDP to be reclassified under appropriate category/subcategory. As per Regulation 7(5) of the FPI Regulations, 2019, foreign portfolio investor is required to have a valid registration as long as it is holding securities or derivatives in India. Regulation 3(1) of the FPI Regulations, 2019 states that no person shall buy, sell or otherwise deal in securities as a foreign portfolio investor unless it has obtained a certificate granted by a designated depository participant on behalf of the Board.\\\\n3. Pursuant to above, adjudication proceedings were initiated and the competent authority appointed the undersigned as the Adjudicating Officer (AO) vide Order dated April 10, 2024 under Section 15-I of SEBI Act, 1992 and Rule 3 of SEBI (Procedure for Holding Inquiry and Imposing Penalties) Rules, 1995 (hereinafter referred to as ' SEBI Adjudication Rules ')  to  inquire  into  and  adjudge  under Section 15A(b) and Section 15HB of the SEBI Act, 1992 for the alleged violation of provisions of Regulation 22(1)(c) of FPI Regulations, 2019 read with Clause 14 of Part A of the Master Circular for Foreign Portfolio Investors, Designated Depository  Participants  and  Eligible  Foreign  Investors,  dated  December  19, 2022;  Regulation  3(1),  Regulation  7(5)  read  with  Regulation  5(a)  of  FPI Regulations, 2019 and Regulation 22(1)(a) of FPI Regulations, 2019 read with Clause 13 of Part A of Master Circular dated December 19, 2022; and Clause 5 of  Third  Schedule  of  Code  of  Conduct  read  with  Regulation  23  of  FPI Regulations, 2019.\\\\n4. A Show Cause Notice (hereafter referred to as ' SCN ') dated April 23, 2024 was issued  to  the  Applicant  in  terms  of  the  provisions  of  Rule  4(1)  of  the  SEBI Adjudication Rules, calling upon the Applicant to show cause as to why an inquiry should not be held and penalty be not imposed upon it, under Section 15A(b)\\\\nand Section 15HB of the SEBI Act, 1992, as applicable for the alleged violations of the aforesaid provisions.\\\\n[2] 5. Pending Adjudication Proceedings, the Applicant proposed to settle the instant proceedings initiated against it, without admitting or denying the findings of facts and  conclusions  of  law,  through  a  settlement  order  and  filed  a  settlement application with SEBI bearing Settlement Application No. 7950/2024 dated June 20, 2024,  in terms  of the  provisions  of  SEBI  (Settlement  Proceedings) Regulations, 2018 (hereinafter referred to as ' Settlement Regulations ').\\\\n6. The  Internal  Committee  (IC)  meeting  was  held  on  August  13,  2024.  Factors enumerated  under  Regulation  10  and  Schedule  II  of SEBI  (Settlement Proceedings)  Regulations,  2018  were  considered  by  the  IC.  The  Internal Committee (IC) recommended ₹64,35,000/- (Rupees Sixty-Four Lakh and ThirtyFive  Thousand  Only)  as  the  monetary  settlement  term.  The  applicant  also submitted  the  revised  settlement  terms  on  August  27,  2024,  in  line  with  the monetary term formulated by the IC. Consequently, the IC recommended the case for settlement. The application was subsequently placed before the High Powered  Advisory  Committee  (HPAC)  on  September  06,  2024.  The  HPAC agreed with the recommendations of the IC and recommended that the request of the applicant for settlement may be accepted.\\\\n7. The Panel of Whole Time Members of SEBI approved the said recommendation of the HPAC on November 06, 2024 and the same was communicated by SEBI to the applicant on November 08, 2024.\\\\n8. Subsequently, the applicant vide email dated November 14, 2024 informed about the remittance of the settlement amount, the receipt of which is confirmed.\\\\n9. Therefore, in view of the acceptance of the settlement terms and the receipt of settlement  amount  as  above  by  SEBI,  the  instant  adjudication  proceedings initiated against Wilmington Trust Collective Investment Trust -\\\\nSettlement Order in respect of Wilmington Trust Collective Investment Trust Lazard/Wilmington ACW Ex-US Equity Advantage Fund\\\\n- Lazard/Wilmington ACW Ex-US Equity Advantage Fund is disposed of in terms of  section  15JB  of  the  SEBI  Act  read  with  regulation  23(1)  of  the  Settlement Regulations on the basis of the settlement terms.\\\\n10. This order is without prejudice to the right of SEBI to take enforcement actions, in  terms of regulation 28 of the Settlement Regulations, including restoring or initiating the proceedings in respect to which the settlement order was passed against the applicant, if:\\\\n- i.  it comes to the notice of the Board that the applicant has not made full and true disclosure;\\\\n- ii.  applicant has violated the undertakings or waivers:\\\\n11. This settlement order is passed on this day of November 21, 2024 and shall come into force with immediate effect.\\\\n12. In terms of regulation 25 of the Settlement Regulations, copies of this order are being sent to the applicant viz. Wilmington Trust Collective Investment Trust Lazard/Wilmington ACW Ex-US Equity Advantage Fund and also to SEBI.\\\\nDate: November 21, 2024\\\\nBARNALI MUKHERJEE ADJUDICATING OFFICER\\\\nPlace: Mumbai\\\\n\\\",\\\"source\\\":{\\\"docId\\\":\\\"clf-hu0mtydifuztqbhb9swt4ser\\\",\\\"title\\\":\\\"November2024/1732191264479.pdf\\\",\\\"url\\\":\\\"/cl/4dc9a4fa-575f-4c18-bf4d-40f5dba3a9d2\\\",\\\"app\\\":\\\"KnowledgeBase\\\",\\\"page_title\\\":\\\"\\\",\\\"entity\\\":\\\"file\\\",\\\"itemId\\\":\\\"9c5b23e1-1184-4e15-989d-2bca0dc2c3b5\\\",\\\"clId\\\":\\\"4dc9a4fa-575f-4c18-bf4d-40f5dba3a9d2\\\"},\\\"confidence\\\":0.29302391994127563,\\\"visibleChunkIndices\\\":[0,1,2]},{\\\"id\\\":\\\"clf-wx3ud5v63iumq3l2z1yj90cx\\\",\\\"content\\\":\\\"Source: Knowledge Base\\\\nFile: Februray2025/1739359654932.pdf\\\\nKnowledge Base ID: de981d90-88dd-436e-b394-9299ecd6ee88\\\\nMime Type: application/pdf\\\\nFile Size: 55932 bytes\\\\nCreated: 4h ago\\\\nUpdated At: 4h ago\\\\nUploaded By: officer1@xyne.local\\\\nContent: [0] Sayyed\\\\n[1] Pratibhuti Vinihit Ltd. & Anr. Knowledge Base\\\\nFile: November2025/1764305359036.pdf\\\\nKnowledge Base ID: e753e310-45d4-4006-a18c-6d463254922b\\\\nMime Type: application/pdf\\\\nFile Size: 399809 bytes\\\\nCreated: 19h ago\\\\nUpdated At: 19h ago\\\\nUploaded By: officer1@xyne.local\\\\nContent: [0] PR No.77/2025\\\\n[1] The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Informal Guidance) Scheme 2003 ( 'IG Scheme, 2003' )  was  issued  on  June  24,  2003  to  enable  certain  entities  to  obtain guidance  from  the  Securities  and  Exchange  Board  of  India  (' Board ')  on  the applicability of laws and regulations administered by it, in the form of 'No Action Letter' or 'Interpretive Letter'.\\\\nThe Board has approved the substitution of the existing IG Scheme, 2003 with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Informal Guidance) Scheme, 2025.\\\\nIn view of the same, with effect from December 01, 2025, the processing of all informal guidance applications shall be governed by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Informal Guidance) Scheme, 2025 ( 'IG Scheme, 2025' ), which broadens the scope of the Scheme  and  enables stock exchanges, clearing corporations, depositories and Managers of Pooled Investment Vehicles registered with the Board, to seek guidance from the Board.\\\\nIt also envisages streamlining and structuring of the process for seeking guidance from the Board, by creation of a nodal cell for processing all informal guidance applications. The salient features of the MoU are as follows:\\\\n1.  To undertake capacity building, development and enhancement of skills of officers of SEBI in the fields of digital forensic, forensic accounting, cyber security etc.\\\\n2.  To design specially tailored courses / training program for SEBI officers to enhance their efficiency and overall output.\\\\n3.  To organize training, seminars, conferences and workshops on topics of mutual interest and invite each other's officers / faculties to participate.\\\\n4.  To use the expertise, facilities and resources available to enhance efficiency and overall output.\\\\n5.  To strengthen the capabilities of SEBI in digital forensics by developing or providing consultancy to develop state-of-the-art infrastructural facilities at SEBI, Mumbai or at any other place as per the requirement of SEBI.\\\\n6.  Specialized  collaborations  like  setting-up  laboratories  in  the  domain  of  cyber security,  digital  forensics,  forensic  accounting,  data  analytics  or  allied  sciences under the consultancy umbrella.\\\\n7.  Subject  to  the  provisions  of  applicable  laws,  both  the  parties  agree  to  share knowledge, which would be useful to the other party in effective discharge of its functions.\\\\nMumbai November 25, 2025\\\\n[2] <div style=\\\\\\\"text-align: center;\\\\\\\">\\\\n  ![image](image_1.png)\\\\n  <span style=\\\\\\\"font-size: 24px; I note that the respondent can only provide information that is available in the records. In this context, I note that the Hon'ble Supreme Court of  India  in Central  Board  of  Secondary  Education  &  Anr.  vs.  Aditya  Bandopadhyay  &  Ors (Judgment dated August 9, 2011) held that 'The RTI Act provides access to all information that is available and existing. This is clear from a combined reading of section 3 and the definitions of `information' and `right to information' under clauses (f) and (j) of section 2 of the Act. If a public authority has any information in the form of data or analysed data, or abstracts, or statistics, an applicant may access such information, subject to the exemptions in section 8 of the Act. But where the  information  sought  is  not  a  part  of  the  record  of  a  public  authority,  and  where  such  information  is  not required  to  be  maintained  under  any  law  or  the  rules  or  regulations  of  the  public  authority,  the  Act  does  not  cast  an obligation  upon  the  public  authority,  to  collect  or  collate  such  non-available  information  and  then  furnish  it  to  an applicant .' Further, I note that the Hon'ble Central Information Commission (hereinafter referred to as ' CIC ') in the matter of Sh. Pattipati Rama Murthy vs. CPIO, SEBI (Decision dated July 8, 2013), held: '… if it (SEBI) does not have any such information in its possession, the CPIO cannot obviously invent  one for the benefit of the Appellant. There is simply no information to be given.' Accordingly, I do not find any deficiency in the response of the respondent.\\n6. do not infer collection-root access from that folder row.\n  - Filtered content ask: for \"answer only from PDF files in Security policies\", first call `ls({ target: { type: \"path\", collectionId: \"kb-1\", path: \"/Policies/Security\" }, depth: 2, metadata: true })`, keep only rows whose `mime_type` is PDF, then call `searchKnowledgeBase({ query: \"exception approval workflow\", filters: { targets: [{ type: \"file\", fileId: \"file-pdf-1\" }, { type: \"file\", fileId: \"file-pdf-2\" }] }, limit: 5 })`.\n  - Known scope ask: if the ask already names the exact KB location, call `searchKnowledgeBase({ query: \"contractor onboarding steps\", filters: { targets: [{ type: \"path\", collectionId: \"kb-1\", path: \"/HR/Onboarding/Checklist.md\" }] }, limit: 5 })`; skip `ls`.\n  - `ls` not useful: if the ask is not about KB, or the exact KB scope is already known and browsing will not improve precision, skip `ls`.\n\n### Public Agent Discipline\n- Call `list_custom_agents` before delegating; log the evaluation and expect it to return `null` when nobody qualifies.\n- Call `runPublicAgent` only after eliminating ambiguity about people, places, and time; restate the resolved entity info before invoking.\n- When list_custom_agents surfaces multiple strong candidates, compare them explicitly before deciding whether to delegate or to keep working with core tools.\n- Prioritize quality over latency; justify why the public agent is required and skip it when core tools can answer faster.\n- Document how the agent result ties back to the user goal and decide whether another follow-up is necessary before moving on.\n- Example: \"Confirmed ACME (US West, RevOps). runPublicAgent(agentName: \"renewal-navigator\", query: \"Summarize ACME renewals in Oct 2024 with blockers and owners\").\"\n\n### Agent Query Crafting\n- Pass explicit agent identifiers plus customized queries; craft one focused query per agent instead of reusing generic text.\n- Enrich queries with clarified scope, dates, and user intents gathered during reasoning to minimize back-and-forth.\n- Record every rewritten query in the reasoning log so reviewers can trace why that agent was triggered.\n- Example: \"runPublicAgent(agentId: \"sales-notes\", query: \"Detail Delta Airlines Q3 forecast confidence after verifying Delta == DAL GTM account\").\"\n\n### Execution Discipline\n- Show proactive drive: after each subtask plan, immediately schedule and run the necessary tools.\n- Combine sequential and parallel tool usage when safe; default to running more than one independent tool per turn.\n- Track dependencies explicitly so you never trigger a child tool before its parent results are analyzed.\n- Prefer the shortest correct tool path; do not insert browsing or discovery steps when a precise search can answer directly.\n\n### Chain-of-Thought Commitment\n- Plan first: picture the end-state, derive minimal subgoals, map tools to each, and weigh independence/dependencies against expected information gain, cost, and latency.\n- For every tool choice, mentally simulate parameter variants; verify schema/limit fit, broaden safe coverage (aliases/entities/scopes/time windows), and consolidate independent lookups into one turn without redundancy.\n- Before committing, run a quick pre-mortem for gaps/failure modes and pick the configuration that maximizes correct coverage per turn; revise if a superior valid parameterization emerges.\n- Examples:\n  - \"What does Alex say about Q4?\" — enumerate Alex identities first, gather IDs, then in one turn query Slack and Gmail with OR-expanded senders plus Q4 synonyms and bounded dates.\n  - \"Build an RCA timeline for last night's outage\" — skim Slack for SEV markers to extract incident keys, then in dependent turns hit Jira with exact keys and Calendar ±2h to stitch the timeline.\n\n### Internal Agent Discipline\n- Internal agents are built-in system agents that are ALWAYS available and do NOT require calling list_custom_agents.\n- Each internal agent provides specific capabilities beyond what core tools can offer.\n- Select internal agents based on capability match, not name familiarity.\n- Use internal agents when core tools or fragment-based retrieval are insufficient.\n- Always follow the expected input format defined for each agent.\n\n### Available Internal Agents\n- agentId: deep_document_agent\n  name: Deep Document Agent\n  capabilities: deep_document_analysis, document_summary, long_context_reading\n  description: Explores a single document intelligently using structured sampling and targeted reading to build a comprehensive understanding.\n  input_format: JSON { userQuery: string, docId: string, startingOffsets?: number[] }\n\n### Usage Guidelines\n- For internal agents: Use run_public_agent directly with the agentId from above.\n- Choose agents based on their capabilities and your task requirements.\n# PLANNING\n- Call toDoWrite at the start of a turn when the plan is new, when review requested changes, or when you need to add or close tasks; otherwise you may proceed without calling toDoWrite to avoid unnecessary iterations.\n- Terminate the active plan the moment you have enough evidence to cater to the complete requirement of the user; immediately drop any remaining subtasks when the goal is satisfied.\n- Scale the number of subtasks to the query’s true complexity , however quality of the final answer and complete execution and satisfaction of user's query outranks task count, you must always prioritize quality\n- Maintain one sub-task per concrete goal; list only the tools truly needed for that sub-task.\n- Only chain subtasks when real dependencies exist—for example, “fetch the people who messaged me today → gather the emails received from them → summarize the combined thread” keeps later steps paused until earlier outputs arrive.\n- After every tool run, immediately update the active sub-task’s status, result, and any newly required tasks so the plan mirrors reality.\n- Never finish a turn after only calling toDoWrite—run at least one execution tool that advances the active task.\n# EXECUTION STRATEGY\n- Work tasks sequentially; complete the current task before starting the next.\n- Call tools with precise parameters tied to the sub-task goal; reuse stored fragments instead of re-fetching data.\n- Run list_custom_agents before run_public_agent; document why the selected agent accelerates the plan.\n- Prefer list_custom_agents → run_public_agent before core tools when justified by the plan.\n- Invoke list_custom_agents at the sub-task level whenever targeted delegation could unlock better results; multi-part queries may require multiple calls as the context evolves.\n- Let earlier tool outputs reshape later sub-tasks (e.g., if getSlackRelatedMessages returns only Finance senders, rewrite the next list_custom_agents query with that Finance focus before proceeding).\n- Obey the `recommendation` flag: pause for clarifications when it reads `clarify_query`, keep collecting data for `gather_more`, and do not progress until a fresh plan is in place for `replan`.\n- If anomalies or notes in the latest review call out missing evidence, misalignments, or unresolved questions, fix those items before progressing and explain the remediation in the plan.\n\n# TOOL CALLS & EXPECTATIONS\n- Use the model's native function/tool-call interface. Provide clean JSON arguments.\n- Do NOT wrap tool calls in custom XML—JAF already handles execution.\n### Agent Delegation Guidelines\n- For INTERNAL agents (listed in system prompt): Use `run_public_agent` directly without calling `list_custom_agents`.\n- For CUSTOM agents (user-defined): MUST call `list_custom_agents` first to discover available agents.\n- If `list_custom_agents` returns `null`, explicitly log that no custom agent was suitable, then proceed with core tools or internal agents.\n- When selecting an agent, compare capabilities and justify why this specific agent is the best fit.\n- Only delegate when a specific agent's documented capabilities make it unquestionably suitable; otherwise keep iterating yourself.\n- After you decide which tools to call, emit a standalone expected-results block summarizing what each tool should achieve:\n<expected_results>\n[\n  {\n    \"toolName\": \"searchGlobal\",\n    \"goal\": \"Find Q4 ARR mentions\",\n    \"successCriteria\": [\"ARR keyword present\", \"Dated Q4\"],\n    \"failureSignals\": [\"No ARR context\"],\n    \"stopCondition\": \"After 2 unsuccessful searches\"\n  }\n]\n</expected_results>\n- Include one entry per tool invocation you intend to make. These expectations feed automatic review, so keep them specific and measurable.\n\n# CONSTRAINT HANDLING\n- When the user requests an action the available tools cannot execute, produce the closest actionable substitute (draft, checklist, instructions) so progress continues.\n- State the exact limitation and what manual follow-up the user must perform to finish.\n\n# FINAL SYNTHESIS\n- Once the run is agentic and research is complete, CALL `synthesize_final_answer` with optional `insightsUsefulForAnswering` guidance when it will help the final answer model emphasize the right conclusions or ordering. This tool composes and streams the response.\n- If the run never became agentic, answer directly instead of calling `synthesize_final_answer`.\n- After calling `synthesize_final_answer`, do not output another user-facing answer in the assistant turn."

The appellant had filed an application (Registration No. SEBIH/R/P/24/00187) dated Nil (received by SEBI on August 17, 2024) under the Right to Information Act, 2005 (“RTI Act”). The respondent, by a letter dated August 27, 2024, responded to the application filed by the appellant. The appellant filed an appeal dated Nil (received by the Office of Appellate Authority on September 23, 2024). I have perused the application, the response of the respondent and the appeal and find that the matter can be decided based on the material available on record.\\\\n\\\\n2. **Request in the application**- The appellant, vide his application dated Nil, *inter alia*, has submitted that he had bought 500 shares of Leaprofin Securities Ltd, however, he is unable to get payment for the same as the registered office of the said company has been closed. The appellant has requested that he may be helped with respect to the aforesaid grievance.\\\\n\\\\n3. **Reply of the Respondent** - The respondent, in response to the application informed that the information sought is in the nature of grievance. Further, the respondent informed that taking action or resolution of grievance does not come under the provisions of RTI Act. Therefore, it does not qualify as information under provisions of section 2(f) of RTI Act. The respondent further informed that investor grievances may be lodged through SCORES and also provided the details of toll free helpline service <hi>number</hi> launched by SEBI to facilitate replies to various queries of the general public on matters relating to securities market\\\\n\\\\n4. **Ground of appeal** - On perusal of the appeal, it appears that the appellant is not satisfied with the response provided by the respondent.\\\\n\\\\nPage 1 of 2\\\\n\\\",\\\"source\\\":{\\\"docId\\\":\\\"clf-stininqvoxfvo82oaf7381ij\\\",\\\"title\\\":\\\"October2024/1729167665827.pdf\\\",\\\"url\\\":\\\"/cl/f767fe84-6cb8-45ae-99b4-b610f50d0cb6\\\",\\\"app\\\":\\\"KnowledgeBase\\\",\\\"page_title\\\":\\\"\\\",\\\"entity\\\":\\\"file\\\",\\\"itemId\\\":\\\"d48a2227-e540-44b9-88d6-29182964649d\\\",\\\"clId\\\":\\\"f767fe84-6cb8-45ae-99b4-b610f50d0cb6\\\"},\\\"confidence\\\":0.3000083292592606,\\\"visibleChunkIndices\\\":[3,1,2]},{\\\"id\\\":\\\"clf-sqerrb1n4t792vrpodxsn0rl\\\",\\\"content\\\":\\\"Source: Knowledge Base\\\\nFile: October2024/1729167594719.pdf\\\\nKnowledge Base ID: f767fe84-6cb8-45ae-99b4-b610f50d0cb6\\\\nMime Type: application/pdf\\\\nFile Size: 407026 bytes\\\\nCreated: 1h ago\\\\nUpdated At: 1h ago\\\\nUploaded By: officer1@xyne.local\\\\nContent: [3] Appeal No. 6170 of 2024\\\\n\\\\n4. **Ground of appeal** - The appellant filed the appeal on the ground that he was refused access to information requested.\\\\n\\\\n5. I have perused the aforesaid request and the response provided thereto. I concur with the response of the respondent that the queries in the application are vague and not specific. It is an established law that the information sought for in order to be disclosable under the RTI Act, must be clear, specific and available in the records of the public authority. In this context, I note that in the matter of *<hi>Mr</hi>. T. V. Sundaresan vs. CPIO, Securities and Exchange Board of India* (Decision dated November 24, 2021), the Hon’ble Central Information Commission (hereinafter referred to as “CIC”) held: “The framework of the RTI Act, 2005 expects that the information sought is specific and believed to be existing with the public authority in documented or material form as such; which can be shared with the appellant as per the provisions of the RTI Act. Answering to broad, multiple and general queries and presumptive documents that should have been generated as per the expectation of the appellant cannot be furnished under the provisions of the Act.” Accordingly, I do not find any deficiency in the response of the respondent.\\\\n\\\\n6. In view of the above observations, I find that there is no need to interfere with the decision of the respondent. The Appeal is accordingly dismissed.\\\\n\\\\nPlace: Mumbai  \\\\nDate: October 17, 2024\\\\n\\\\nRUCHI CHOJER  \\\\nAPPELLATE AUTHORITY UNDER THE RTI ACT  \\\\nSECURITIES AND EXCHANGE BOARD OF INDIA\\\\n\\\\nPage 2 of 2\\\\n[1] 1. The respondent also provided the details of the toll free helpline service <hi>numbers</hi> launched by SEBI to facilitate replies to various queries of the general public on matters relating to securities market.\\\\n\\\\n4. **Ground of appeal** – The appellant has filed the appeal on the ground that he was refused access to information requested.\\\\n\\\\n5. I have perused the application and the response provided thereto. On consideration, I concur with the response of the respondent that query of the appellant is more in the nature of grievance/complaint. I note that redressal of grievance does not come under the purview of the RTI Act. In this context, I note that the Hon’ble Central Information Commission, in the matter of *<hi>Mr</hi>. Surendra Vishwakarma vs. President Secretariat* (Order dated April 29, 2016) observed that “*In this context, we note that the RTI Act cannot be used to make the respondent to do certain things or take certain action for the reason that the Act is not the proper law for redressal of grievances/disputes and there are other appropriate forum(s) for resolving such matters.*” Notwithstanding the same, I note that the respondent has appropriately guided the appellant to refer to the SCORES website for lodging his grievance, if any, and also provided helpline service <hi>numbers</hi> launched by SEBI, to facilitate replies to various queries of the general public on matters relating to securities market. In view of the same, I find that the application has been adequately addressed and no further intervention is warranted at this stage.\\\\n\\\\n6. In view of the above observations, I find that there is no need to interfere with the decision of the respondent.
